question.problem: Find the area bounded by the polar curve $r=2-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ for $\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \pi .$
question.worked_solution:
The area bounded by a polar curve is given by

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}(\theta )\text{d}\theta \,.
$$

When $r(\theta )=2-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $, ${\theta }_{1}=\frac{\pi }{2}$ and ${\theta }_{2}=\pi $, this gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }(2-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }(4-8\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +4{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(4\theta \,{|}_{\pi /2}^{\pi }+8\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,{|}_{\pi /2}^{\pi }-2{\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }(-1+\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta ))\,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(4\theta \,{|}_{\pi /2}^{\pi }+8\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,{|}_{\pi /2}^{\pi }-2(-\theta \,{|}_{\pi /2}^{\pi }+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )}{2}\,{|}_{\pi /2}^{\pi })) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(4\theta \,{|}_{\pi /2}^{\pi }+8\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,{|}_{\pi /2}^{\pi }+2\theta \,{|}_{\pi /2}^{\pi }-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )\,{|}_{\pi /2}^{\pi }) \\  & =3\theta \,{|}_{\pi /2}^{\pi }+4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,{|}_{\pi /2}^{\pi }-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )}{2}\,{|}_{\pi /2}^{\pi } \\  & =3(\pi -\frac{\pi }{2})+4(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}))-\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )) \\  & =\frac{3\pi }{2}+4\cdot (-1)-\frac{1}{2}(0) \\  & =\frac{3\pi }{2}-4 \\  & =\frac{3\pi -8}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
